titleStmt.title: Coxswain Recording of the 1997 Record Breaking Win by the National Men's Team at the Head of The Charles RegattaThe Head of the Charles Regatta is one of the world’s most prestigious and celebrated rowing events, bringing together elite athletes and teams from across the globe to compete on Boston’s iconic Charles River.

publicationStmt.p: Source, Row2k.com— The following is a transcript from a 1997 recording of the coxswain Pete Cipollone. The source provided both the recording and transcript.

sourceDesc.p: Row2k.com is an online publication source for major and minor rowing news: covering photography, race results, interviews, live reports, and more on the national, collegiate, and youth rowing levels.

div.head: Practice: at the starting line before the race begins
div.p: Fi' chaaCoxswains often use different calls, phrases, or sounds to motivate their rowers depending on the circumstance and what the rower may need at that point of the race.

Eight -Cipollone is counting the number of strokes. In this case, he is counting because the rowers are performing strokes with a certain technique or goal in mind; aka "a foucused (insert any number)". Example: when the rowers aren't pushing hard enough with their legs, the coxswain will call for a focused 10 for legs which means that each rower needs to realign with their technique and the amount of strength they are exerting from their legs.
in two we shiftwhen rowers "shift" it refers to either increasing or decreasing (in this case, increasing) the pace of the stroke
One we're at 3636 is their pace
We got crews around, paddlerow lightly/with less strength paddle.
Give us a little room, Penn...

Weigh enoughIn rowing, “weigh enough” is a traditional call from the coxswain telling the rowers to stop rowing and let their oars rest on the water., watch the oars on port side... ok all eight ready, go.
Ok, how do you guys feel on warmup? Everybody's ready?

div.head: Beginning of race

div.head: End of Race
div.p: Guys, listen up, 12:40 down, I think you can break the fucking record!

p.hi: The team comes in first, breaking the record for Men's 8+s in this division at Head of the CHarles Regatta --- at 32 year old race at this point.
